overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the run misses the one positive segment because its only identified finding is low confidence; at all identified confidence levels it detects the segment correctly.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: Strict scoring records zero true positives at every threshold: the occurrence is correctly localized and mechanistically complete but uses a near-neighbor label instead of Averaging Bias.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first scoring records one true positive at all identified confidence levels and at the candidate-inclusive threshold, with no instance false positive until the three negative-segment candidates enter.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The three candidates are useful abstentions for analysis review, but candidate-inclusive scoring appropriately exposes their false-alarm cost because each is localized to a ground-truth negative segment.

overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run demonstrates a taxonomy and confidence tradeoff: the RAG recognized the hidden mechanism but did not name the exact target label, and its conservative low-confidence decision suppresses detection at the recommended threshold. Candidate handling is informative but reduces precision when candidate findings are promoted into the detection tier.
